author: claude
headline: Two windy spells to plan around at UK and North Sea ports this week
standfirst: Gusts near crane limits hit Felixstowe and Southampton on Monday and return across the Channel and North Sea from Friday. A deep Atlantic low will hold up ships from North America by 1–2 days. Maersk lifts its UK fuel surcharge to 20%.

port_notes.felixstowe: Gusts to 16 m/s from 12:00 to 21:00 on Monday may pause cranes. Move Monday afternoon collections to Tuesday morning if you can, and allow 12–24 hours on anything booked tight.
port_notes.southampton: Two short gusty spells on Monday and Tuesday, then a longer one on Friday from 10:00 to 22:00. Keep Friday bookings flexible and allow 12–24 hours.
port_notes.london_gateway: The worst of the week here: gusts to 19 m/s from Friday 16:00 to Saturday 14:00. Tell your haulier now and move Friday evening and Saturday collections to early Friday or Monday.
port_notes.liverpool: No crane or pilotage limits forecast all week. A good week to clear releases: speak to your carrier about release and delivery now.
port_notes.rotterdam: An hour near crane limits on Tuesday evening, then a gustier spell from Saturday 14:00. If you tranship here, confirm weekend feeder connections and allow 12–24 hours.
port_notes.antwerp: Brief gusts on Tuesday afternoon, then Friday 13:00 to 20:00 and again from Saturday afternoon. Allow 12–24 hours on Friday and weekend moves.
port_notes.bremerhaven: Gusty again on Tuesday from 09:00 to 13:00 and late on Saturday. Allow 12–24 hours on Tuesday vessel calls and avoid tight cut-offs.
port_notes.hamburg: Gusts near crane limits on Tuesday from 08:00 to 15:00 and late on Saturday. Allow 12–24 hours on Tuesday and keep weekend plans flexible.

inbound_note: A deep low in the mid-North Atlantic brings seas of 6 m and gusts near 30 m/s on Tuesday and Wednesday. Ships from North America crossing in that window are likely to arrive 1–2 days late. Don't book haulage against the published ETA; confirm the revised ETA with your carrier before you commit.

sections.ports: Seven of the eight ports see at least one spell of gusts near crane limits this week, in two waves. The first runs from Monday to Tuesday. The second, stronger one arrives on Friday and lasts into Sunday, with London Gateway most exposed.
sections.lanes: Only the mid-North Atlantic is rough enough to slow ships this week.
sections.reliability: Sea-Intelligence puts August global schedule reliability at 49.9%, down 5.9 points on July and 15.2 points on a year earlier. Late ships arrived 6.81 days behind schedule on average. Xeneta measures 29% for the same month. The 20.9-point gap comes from method: Sea-Intelligence counts an arrival as on time within one day of schedule, Xeneta only on the scheduled day. Both rank Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd first and second. For planning, assume about half of arrivals will miss their scheduled day and keep delivery promises loose.
sections.advisories: Maersk has raised its fuel surcharge for the UK and Ireland to 20% and has raised its S5S contingency surcharge. MSC has restored a direct service from Karachi to seven European ports. Hapag-Lloyd has suspended bookings to the Philippines because of port congestion there and announced a North America GRI. CMA CGM adds a reefer surcharge from Northern Europe to Latin America.
